notes: Use a Touch 'n Go card for the LRT and MRT; Grab taxis are cheap (5-15 MYR within the city). The KLIA Ekspres takes 28 minutes and costs 55 MYR.
Summer (June-September) is relatively dry, but expect 33°C and humidity. Afternoon downpours are common, so sightsee in the morning.
Malaysian food blends three cultures: nasi lemak (Malay), char kway teow (Chinese) and roti canai (Indian). Mamak restaurants are open 24 hours.
Shoulders and knees must be covered in mosques and Hindu temples. At Batu Caves, monkeys snatch bags.
Petronas Skybridge tickets sell out days ahead; KL Tower is an alternative with better views.
Alcohol is expensive because of tax. Tipping is not expected, and a 10% service charge is added.

transit.name: Touch 'n Go Card
transit.why_chosen: Works on the LRT, MRT, monorail and buses; the KLIA Ekspres is separate
transit.coverage: Rapid KL tüm hatlar, RapidKL otobüs

stops.name: Petronas Twin Towers Skybridge
stops.tips: Skybridge on the 41st floor plus the 86th-floor observation deck (~98 MYR). Tickets sell out online days ahead, so book the first morning slot.

stops.name: KLCC Park
stops.tips: Park and fountain at the foot of the towers; the best spot for photos of them.

stops.name: Nasi Lemak Wanjo Kampung Baru
stops.tips: A nasi lemak classic in Kampung Baru, with sambal and chicken, within walking distance of KLCC.

stops.name: Kampung Baru
stops.tips: A Malay village in the middle of the skyscrapers, with wooden houses and street stalls.

stops.name: KL Tower Sky Deck
stops.tips: Menara KL's glass box and sunset views; the best place to see the Petronas Towers from across the city.

backups.name: Suria KLCC Signatures Food Court
backups.tips: Mall food court; try the laksa and satay.

backups.name: Aquaria KLCC
backups.tips: Aquarium beneath the convention centre; a good rainy-day option.

stops.name: Batu Caves
stops.tips: 30 minutes by KTM train. 272 colourful steps, a giant Murugan statue, and monkeys to watch out for. Cool and quiet in the morning.

stops.name: Petaling Street
stops.tips: Chinatown market with fake designer bags and street food; haggle.

stops.name: Hong Kee Claypot Chicken Rice
stops.tips: Charcoal-cooked claypot rice on Petaling Street; expect a queue at lunch.

stops.name: Sri Mahamariamman Temple
stops.tips: KL's oldest Hindu temple, with a colourful gopuram.

stops.name: Central Market Kuala Lumpur
stops.tips: Art deco market selling batik and handicrafts, and air-conditioned.

backups.name: Kim Lian Kee Hokkien Mee
backups.tips: Hokkien mee since 1927, on Petaling Street.

stops.name: Merdeka Square
stops.tips: Independence square and the Sultan Abdul Samad Building; lovely in morning light.

stops.name: Masjid Jamek
stops.tips: Moorish-style mosque where two rivers meet; admire it from outside during non-visiting hours.

stops.name: River of Life Walk
stops.tips: Restored riverside walkway along the Klang, with blue-lit fountains.

stops.name: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia
stops.tips: Asia's best Islamic art museum: air-conditioned, with domes and calligraphy.

stops.name: Jalan Alor
stops.tips: Bukit Bintang's street food strip: grilled seafood, satay and char kway teow. It comes alive in the evening.

backups.name: Pavilion KL Food Court
backups.tips: Food court in the Bukit Bintang mall; good in the rain.

backups.name: Perdana Botanical Garden
backups.tips: The city's botanical park, with an orchid garden; an alternative to the museum.

stops.name: Brickfields Little India
stops.tips: Colourful Indian neighbourhood with temples and flower garlands.

stops.name: Thean Hou Temple
stops.tips: Six-tier Chinese temple on a hilltop, with red lanterns and city views.

stops.name: Vishal Food & Catering Brickfields
stops.tips: South Indian food served on a banana leaf; eat with your hands.

stops.name: Bangsar Village
stops.tips: Stylish neighbourhood with cafés and boutiques.

stops.name: Bangsar Devi's Corner
stops.tips: Roti canai and teh tarik at a 24-hour mamak.

backups.name: National Museum of Malaysia
backups.tips: National museum on Malaysian history; good in the rain.

stops.name: Dutch Square Melaka
stops.tips: 2 hours by bus from KL (~15 MYR). Red Stadthuys and Christ Church, UNESCO-listed.

stops.name: A Famosa
stops.tips: The gate of the Portuguese fort and St. Paul's Hill, with views over the Strait of Malacca.

stops.name: Jonker Street
stops.tips: Peranakan antique shops and cafés; night market at weekends.

stops.name: Hoe Kee Chicken Rice Ball
stops.tips: Melaka's signature chicken rice, with rice shaped into balls; the queue moves fast.

stops.name: Baba & Nyonya Heritage Museum
stops.tips: Peranakan mansion, visited on a guided tour.

backups.name: Nancy's Kitchen Melaka
backups.tips: Nyonya cuisine; try the ayam pongteh.

backups.name: Melaka River Cruise
backups.tips: River boat ride; an alternative to the museum.

stops.name: Genting Skyway
stops.tips: From Awana, one of the world's longest cable cars climbs to 1,800 m. Enjoy the cool mountain air and a stop at Chin Swee Temple.

stops.name: Genting SkyAvenue Food Court
stops.tips: Food court in the mall on the mountain.

stops.name: Chin Swee Caves Temple
stops.tips: Taoist temple on a cliff, at the cable car's mid-station.

stops.name: Skytropolis Genting
stops.tips: Indoor theme park, unaffected by rain.

backups.name: Sekinchan Rice Fields
backups.tips: Rice fields near Kuala Selangor; best in harvest season.

stops.name: Masjid Negara
stops.tips: National mosque with a blue star-shaped dome; robes are lent to visitors during visiting hours.

stops.name: Kuala Lumpur Railway Station
stops.tips: Historic Moorish-style station; good for photos.

stops.name: Restoran Yut Kee
stops.tips: Hainan coffee and roti babi since 1928; a fitting farewell lunch.

stops.name: KL Sentral
stops.tips: KLIA Ekspres takes 28 minutes; time to say goodbye.

backups.name: KL Bird Park
backups.tips: The world's largest free-flight walk-in aviary; an alternative to the mosque.
